model.official_repo: https://github.com/CAIC-AD/YOLOPv2 — paper arXiv:2208.11434 'YOLOPv2: Better, Faster, Stronger for Panoptic Driving Perception' (Han et al., T3CAIC). Single multi-task net, three heads. TorchScript forward returns [pred,anchor_grid], seg, ll in that order (verified demo.py). seg=drivable-area (2-ch, argmax), ll=lane-line (the head we want).
model.license: MIT (LICENSE file: 'MIT License', Copyright (c) 2022 CAIC-AD). README confirms 'released under the MIT Licence'. Fully usable/redistributable for a university IGVC robot; only obligation is retaining the copyright+license notice — keep LICENSE alongside the weights. CAVEAT: weights were trained on BDD100K, whose dataset terms (research-framed) — not the MIT code license — would be the binding constraint if anyone ever asked about COMMERCIAL use. Non-issue for academic IGVC.
model.trained_on: BDD100K — 100k forward-facing windshield/dashcam clips of US road driving (70k train / 10k val / 20k test). Lane head learned PAINTED ROAD LANE MARKINGS seen from a car windshield with a horizon/vanishing point. BDD100K lane GT preprocessing: centerline of the 2 annotated lines, drawn 8 px wide for TRAIN, 2 px wide for TEST. Output is binary lane/no-lane (paper: C=2 for both seg tasks, but the LANE head is decoded as single-channel — see outputs). In-domain lane IoU is only ~27.25% (Table 4) — already marginal even on its own distribution.
weights_torchscript_urls: https://github.com/CAIC-AD/YOLOPv2/releases/download/V0.0.1/yolopv2.pt — CANONICAL. GitHub release asset, tag V0.0.1, 156,380,200 bytes (~149.1 MiB), FP32 TorchScript (torch.jit.load, NOT a state_dict). Verify byte count after download. https://huggingface.co/spaces/hank1996/yolopv2 — HuggingFace Gradio DEMO Space (not a direct weight download, but the .pt is mirrored inside the Space repo). Use only as a fallback mirror; the GitHub release is canonical.

onnx_sources.url: https://github.com/hpc203/yolopv2-opencv-onnxrun-cpp-py/blob/main/onnxruntime/onnx_post/main.py — 54 models on Baidu pan (CN-hosted, hard to fetch). Three flavors: onnx/ (raw 3 maps), onnx_split/ (decoded+cat), onnx_post/ (NMS baked).
onnx_sources.notes: Best torch-free decode pattern: lane = np.squeeze(results[1]); mask = np.where(lane>0.5,1,0).astype(uint8); cv2.resize NEAREST to orig. seg = np.argmax(np.squeeze(results[0],0),axis=0). Confirms ll is sigmoid prob in [0,1] (>0.5 == torch.round). In THIS port ll is at index 1 (post-surgery graph).

preprocessing.recommended_input_hw: 384x640 (HxW) — the authors' native test resolution and the only res where the official [12:372] crop is exactly valid. If you adopt the PINTO/ONNX plain-resize path (no letterbox crop), 288x480 is the closest pre-exported match to our 480x300 frame; for an export-it-yourself path, fix the input to 384x640. Decide stretch-vs-letterbox ONCE and never mix the two math paths.
preprocessing.color_order: RGB. cv_bridge hands you BGR uint8 HxWx3 (our Pipeline contract input). The reference does img[:, :, ::-1] (BGR->RGB) — this flip is REQUIRED, do not skip it.
preprocessing.normalization: /255.0 ONLY. NO ImageNet mean/std. Verified identical in CAIC-AD demo.py (img/=255.0), PINTO demo, hpc203 demo, Kazuhito00 sample. Detection feature maps need a sigmoid in decode, but you skip detection entirely.
preprocessing.letterbox: Original .pt path: letterbox(img, new_shape=(640,640), color=(114,114,114), auto=True, scaleFill=False, scaleup=True, stride=32). auto=True pads to nearest stride-32 multiple (dw,dh = np.mod(dw,stride); each /=2; top/bottom = round(dh-/+0.1)). For a FIXED-input ONNX/TRT engine you MUST call letterbox with auto=False (or just cv2.resize stretch). RECOMMENDED for our 480x300: letterbox to 384x640 keep-aspect (pad 114) so the official [12:372] crop is valid AND aspect is preserved (asphalt tape geometry matters for the costmap reprojection). Track (dw,dh) and r to invert later. ALTERNATIVE (simpler, what the ONNX demos do): plain cv2.resize stretch to (W,H) and DROP the crop — accept mild aspect distortion.
preprocessing.dtype: float32 (laptop CPU ORT and Jetson CUDA EP). On Jetson with TensorRT FP16 EP you can hand float32 in and let trt_fp16_enable do the cast, OR feed float16 to halve host->device memcpy. np.ascontiguousarray(...) after the transpose is mandatory or ORT may copy/error.

outputs.all_outputs: DEPENDS ON THE EXPORT — you MUST introspect session.get_outputs() [(o.name,o.shape) for o in ...] at load time. Two confirmed export families: (A) PINTO surgically-renamed graph: seg(1,2,H,W), ll(1,1,H,W), pred0(1,255,H/8,W/8), pred1(1,255,H/16,W/16), pred2(1,255,H/32,W/32) — ll is at NAME 'll'. (B) Kazuhito00 raw torch.onnx.export flatten: 6 outputs, results[0]=det(3 maps packed), results[1..3]=anchor_grid0/1/2, results[4]=seg, results[5]=ll. hpc203 post-graph: results[0]=seg(2ch), results[1]=ll(1ch), results[2..4]=det. NEVER hardcode an index — match by name 'll' if present, else fall back to the 1-channel HxW output that is not the 2-channel seg.
outputs.lane_output_index: By NAME: 'll'. By position it is export-specific (PINTO/hpc203: 1; Kazuhito00: 5). Resolution rule for yolopv2.py: pick the output whose name=='ll', else the output with shape (1,1,H,W) i.e. channel dim==1, else if only (1,2,H,W) exists treat as hustvl/YOLOP-style and argmax channel-1. Log the chosen name+shape once at startup.
outputs.lane_output_shape: (1,1,H,W) for canonical YOLOPv2 (single-channel sigmoid prob). The (1,2,H,W) figure floating around the web is from the OLDER hustvl/YOLOP model and from YOLOPv2's DRIVABLE-AREA head — NOT the YOLOPv2 lane head. Confirmed by official torch.round(...).squeeze(1) (squeeze(1) on a size-2 axis would error) and by hpc203 np.squeeze(results[1]) collapsing to (H,W).
outputs.lane_threshold: 0.5. Official torch path: torch.round(ll) == (ll>=0.5) on a [0,1] sigmoid map. hpc203 numpy path: np.where(ll>0.5,1,0). Practically identical (half-point is measure-zero on continuous sigmoid). The lane head output is ALREADY post-sigmoid (in [0,1]) — that is the ONLY reason torch.round is valid; do NOT apply sigmoid again. VERIFY on the laptop with CPU ORT: print(ll.min(), ll.max()) — if in [0,1] the round path is correct as-is; if it spans ~[-10,10] it is raw logits and you must sigmoid first (set already_sigmoid=False). NOTE the detection maps pred0/1/2 ARE raw logits and need sigmoid — but you skip detection. conf-thres 0.3 / iou-thres 0.45 are detection-NMS only — irrelevant to lanes.

design.postprocess_to_mask: STEP-BY-STEP (the byte-exact contract for run()). PATH A — official letterbox-to-384x640 (decode-faithful, recommended): (1) letterbox the 480x300 BGR to 384x640 keep-aspect (pad 114), record r (scale) and (dw,dh) pad. (2) BGR->RGB, HWC->CHW, /255, ascontiguousarray, float32, add batch -> (1,3,384,640). (3) run session; grab the 'll' output (1,1,384,640) by NAME. (4) prob = ll[0,0] (already sigmoid, [0,1]); DO NOT apply the official [12:372] crop here UNLESS your output is at the exact 360->720 geometry of the original 1280x720 LoadImages pipeline — for a clean 384x640 ll output skip the crop and instead remove the letterbox pad directly: rows/cols corresponding to (dw,dh). (5) bin = (prob > 0.5).astype(uint8). (6) Remove letterbox padding: crop bin to the unpadded region [round(dh):H-round(dh), round(dw):W-round(dw)]. (7) cv2.resize the cropped bin back to the ORIGINAL frame size (480x300, i.e. (W=480,H=300)) with INTER_NEAREST to keep it binary. (8) Build class-id mask: mask = bin * class_id_lane (class_id_lane=1). everything-else stays 0. (9) confidence = (prob_unpadded_resized * 255).astype(uint8) (resize prob with INTER_LINEAR for a smooth confidence channel — the reference demo discards prob, so this is OUR design freedom for the kiwicampus layer). (10) If the node downstream resizes to the ORGANIZED CLOUD shape (height>1, e.g. 256x448 COMPACT per CLAUDE.md), do the final cv2.resize to the cloud HxW instead of 480x300 so mask HxW == cloud HxW (kiwicampus contract requires mask and cloud share shape AND header.stamp). PATH B — plain stretch (simpler, what ONNX demos do): cv2.resize 480x300 -> (W,H) of model, no pad; decode prob=ll[0,0]>0.5; cv2.resize NEAREST straight back to 480x300/cloud shape; NO crop, NO unletterbox. Mild aspect distortion. NEVER mix Path A's [12:372]/x2 math with Path B. The [12:372] crop + scale_factor=2 is hardcoded to the original 1280x720->384 letterbox geometry and is silent garbage on any other input geometry.

jetson.onnxruntime_gpu_wheel: Do NOT pip install onnxruntime-gpu from PyPI (x86_64/win only — no aarch64; you'll get ['AzureExecutionProvider','CPUExecutionProvider'] = no GPU). Use the NVIDIA Jetson AI Lab index keyed jp6/cu126 (JetPack 6 + CUDA 12.6, Python 3.10/cp310 ONLY): wget https://pypi.jetson-ai-lab.dev/jp6/cu126/+f/f6e/2baa664069470/onnxruntime_gpu-1.20.2-cp310-cp310-linux_aarch64.whl then pip3 install it. Newer wheels (1.23.0, 1.24.0 cp310 aarch64) on the same index. FIRST: pip uninstall onnxruntime onnxruntime-gpu (same package name — CPU build shadows GPU). Dev laptop stays CPU onnxruntime 1.23 for offline validation. Bake a startup check: import onnxruntime as ort; assert 'CUDAExecutionProvider' in ort.get_available_providers() — fail fast if only Azure/CPU show (= wrong wheel).
jetson.fp16: Enable FP16 — Orin tensor cores. TensorRT EP: 'trt_fp16_enable': True (env equiv ORT_TENSORRT_FP16_ENABLE=1, default 0). Pragmatic recommendation: CUDAExecutionProvider FP16 may be the better DEFAULT for field reliability — zero engine-build wall time, no cache-invalidation foot-guns on reboots. Use the TRT EP only once model+SDK are FROZEN and you've validated the engine cache survives reboots. Either way the seg model is real-time on Orin. VALIDATE the mask is identical between laptop-CPU-fp32 and Jetson-fp16 on a fixed frame before trusting (fp16 can shift the 0.5 threshold on borderline pixels).
jetson.expected_latency: No published YOLOPv2-Orin benchmark exists (flagged). Reasoned from comparable CSPDarknet seg nets: YOLO-nano FP16 on AGX Orin ~2.6ms, Orin NX ~4.1ms; YOLOPv2 paper hits 91 FPS on a V100 at 640x384. Estimate the YOLOPv2 forward pass at ~8-20ms (~50-120 FPS) on Orin at 384x640 FP16 — comfortably under the camera's 15 fps (~66ms) budget; our 480x300 input is even cheaper. The network is NOT the bottleneck — preprocess/postprocess numpy + host<->device memcpy + ROS/costmap plumbing are. Set MAXN + jetson_clocks for the competition run (lower power modes are 2-4x slower).
jetson.gotchas: (1) numpy<2 MANDATORY on Jetson — cv2/onnxruntime are NumPy-1.x-ABI; numpy 2.x crashes the import. Pin numpy~=1.26; re-check after any pip install (CuPy/torch can silently bump it). yolopv2.py must use the NumPy-1.x common subset (the decode only uses np.squeeze/np.where/astype/cv2.resize — all version-agnostic). (2) Prefer apt python3-opencv; do NOT pip install opencv-python alongside cv_bridge (ABI clash). (3) CAP THE ORT CPU THREAD POOL: SessionOptions intra_op_num_threads=1, inter_op_num_threads=1 — otherwise ORT grabs all cores and starves the 20Hz MPPI loop + EKF + kiwicampus layer (RViz-on-Jetson already pushed load 10.75/8 and starved MPPI per CLAUDE.md). (4) Run 1-3 WARMUP inferences on a dummy frame after InferenceSession before declaring the node ready — TRT first run can take tens of seconds to MINUTES building the engine (cache cuts 384s->9s on reload). (5) Delete trt_cache/ on ANY SDK/ORT/TRT/hardware change — engines are non-portable and a stale engine silently misbehaves. (6) Export with FIXED input (no dynamic axes) so TRT builds exactly ONE engine. (7) ZED runs in the zed_wrapper process, perception_node is SEPARATE — so ZED's CUDA context and ORT's are in different processes (no shared-context corruption), but they share Orin unified VRAM (ZED NEURAL_LIGHT + TRT engine + costmaps) — watch memory. Keep them separate processes; do NOT composable-compose perception into the ZED container.

domain_gap.evidence: YOLOPv2's lane head is BDD100K-only (forward windshield/dashcam US road lanes, 8px-train/2px-test painted centerlines, horizon + vanishing point) with ZERO cross-domain evaluation in the paper. In-DOMAIN lane IoU is already only 27.25% (Table 4) — the high 87.3% 'accuracy' is dominated by background. Our scene is the structural opposite: ZED at ~15deg down-tilt looking ACROSS the surface at 3-inch white TAPE boundaries, NO vanishing point, lines curving laterally; IGVC 2026 rules put the course on GRASS (white-on-grass), and the team's asphalt pad is only the practice surface. Neither matches BDD100K asphalt-road texture. Lane-detection domain-adaptation literature explicitly warns of 'severe performance decrease' on unseen domains. Adoption is real but ALL documented usage is dashcam/road AD — zero robotics-on-grass/IGVC deployments found; the two embedded ports found (TI TDA4VM, Axelera) both hit trouble at the lane-output stage ('Lane Line Detection distortion'). The team's own memory note (adaptive_lane_params_finalized) already concluded 'no pretrained model fits IGVC tape' and deferred ONNX — this research SUPPORTS that.
domain_gap.most_likely_failure: Low-recall, broken/sparse lane masks: fires intermittently on the cleanest white segments and DROPS the boundary through curves, dashes, grass texture, and the off-axis low-tilt geometry it never saw. A FLICKERING lane mask feeding the kiwicampus semantic layer produces intermittent LETHAL cells (the repo already fights costmap lane flicker) and gaps in a boundary let the planner cut the course -> potential DQ. Secondary: white false positives on barrels/tents/sky reflections the road-lane prior was never trained to reject.
domain_gap.mitigation: Cheapest->most-expensive: (1) FREE: ROI-crop to the lower ground-plane band before inference (top ~30-45% is sky/tents/horizon = pure false-positive fuel for a model with no horizon prior; helps classical too — reuse existing overlay_roi30/80 experiments). (2) CHEAP+ROBUST: keep the classical adaptive-threshold pipeline as PRIMARY and use YOLOPv2 only as a confirming VOTE (logical AND to kill classical's grass/glare false positives, or OR only where classical confidence is low) — never let the raw NN mask drive the costmap alone. (3) COSTLY (real fix): fine-tune a SMALL net (TwinLiteNet+ Nano 34k params, or a tiny U-Net) on a few hundred auto-labeled-from-classical + hand-corrected IGVC frames — NOT full 38.9M-param YOLOPv2 (tiny-dataset fine-tune risks catastrophic forgetting of its only asset). DECISION: stock YOLOPv2 on IGVC tape is a curiosity/science-fair demo, not a competition lane source; the shippable improvement remains classical-adaptive + ROI-crop + locked ZED exposure already in the stack.

params_to_expose: onnx_model_path (path to the .onnx; default the 384x640 or 288x480 file)
already_sigmoid (default True; flip to False if a custom export strips the lane sigmoid)
preprocess_mode ('letterbox_384x640' vs 'stretch' — pick ONE, don't mix decode math)
input_hw (H,W the model expects; introspect/validate against session.get_inputs())
ep_providers (ordered list; default Jetson TRT->CUDA->CPU, laptop CPU)
roi_top_frac (ROI crop fraction, default ~0.35 — domain-gap mitigation)
output_resize_to ('frame' 480x300 vs 'cloud' HxW so mask matches the organized cloud for kiwicampus)
min_area (optional connected-component cleanup — NOTE: NOT part of the reference decode, it adds none; this is OUR addition matching the existing classical pipeline's min_area=80)
integration.cpu_gpu_notes: GPU/TRT carries the conv math (the expensive 90%+), freeing CPU of inference. BUT residual CPU per frame = preprocess (resize/letterbox, BGR->RGB, /255, transpose, ascontiguousarray), host<->device memcpy, postprocess (threshold, unletterbox, cv2.resize, class-id remap). On the saturated Orin these run on the same starved cores feeding MPPI/EKF/kiwicampus — so (a) cap intra/inter_op_num_threads=1, (b) keep numpy ops minimal, (c) keep the session single-threaded (don't share across ROS executor threads; ORT CUDA-Graphs cannot be invoked from multiple threads on one session). Do all decode in float32/uint8 with the version-agnostic numpy subset so the same code runs on laptop numpy>=2 and Jetson numpy<2.
integration.risks: HIGHEST: output index/channel mismatch -> silent garbage. The ONNX output ORDER and the lane channel count are EXPORT-SPECIFIC (PINTO ll@'ll' 1ch; Kazuhito00 ll@index5; hpc203 ll@index1). MUST resolve by introspecting session.get_outputs() names+shapes at load, log the chosen ('ll', shape), and assert channel==1 (or argmax-fallback for a 2ch hustvl-style export). SECOND: applying the official [12:372] crop + x2 upsample to a non-1280x720 geometry -> garbage; only valid for the exact original letterbox path. THIRD: mask HxW must EQUAL the organized-cloud HxW and share header.stamp, cloud must be organized (height>1), and LabelInfo must be transient_local+reliable or the kiwicampus layer silently ignores frames (per CLAUDE.md). FOURTH: fp16 vs fp32 can flip borderline 0.5 pixels — validate mask parity laptop-vs-Jetson. FIFTH: domain gap (see domain_gap) — do not let stock weights drive the costmap solo.

design.reference_decode_numpy:
def decode_lane_mask(outputs, output_names, orig_hw, *,
                     lane_threshold=0.5, lane_class_id=1,
                     already_sigmoid=True, letterbox_pad=None):
    """
    Torch-free YOLOPv2 lane-line decode (numpy + opencv only).
    Works on numpy<2 (Jetson) and numpy>=2 (laptop): only np.squeeze/np.where/
    np.exp/astype/cv2.resize are used.

    outputs       : list of np.ndarray returned by ort_session.run(None, feeds)
    output_names   : [o.name for o in ort_session.get_outputs()]  (same order)
    orig_hw        : (H, W) you want the mask AT (the 480x300 frame, or the
                     organized-cloud HxW so mask shape == cloud shape).
    letterbox_pad  : None for the plain-stretch path; else (dw, dh, r) from the
                     keep-aspect letterbox so we remove pad before resize.

    Returns (mask_uint8 HxW of class ids: lane=lane_class_id else 0,
             conf_uint8 HxW: lane probability * 255).
    """
    import numpy as np
    import cv2

    # --- 1. Pick the lane ('ll') output by NAME, else by shape. NEVER hardcode
    #        an index: the order is export-specific (PINTO ll-by-name / index 1,
    #        Kazuhito00 index 5, hpc203 index 1). ---
    ll = None
    for name, arr in zip(output_names, outputs):
        if name == 'll' or name.lower().endswith('lane') or 'lane' in name.lower():
            ll = arr
            break
    if ll is None:
        # fallback: the single-channel (1,1,H,W) output that is not the 2-ch seg
        cands = [a for a in outputs if a.ndim == 4 and a.shape[1] == 1]
        if not cands:
            # last resort: a (1,2,H,W) hustvl-style export -> argmax channel 1
            two = [a for a in outputs if a.ndim == 4 and a.shape[1] == 2]
            if not two:
                raise ValueError('no lane-like output found; introspect the onnx')
            seg2 = np.squeeze(two[0], axis=0)          # (2,H,W)
            prob = seg2[1]                              # lane channel
            already_sigmoid = True                     # argmax-style; treat as prob
            ll = prob[None, None]                      # normalize to (1,1,H,W)
        else:
            ll = cands[0]

    # --- 2. To a 2D prob map in [0,1]. YOLOPv2 lane head is single-channel and
    #        ALREADY sigmoid (that is why the official decode uses torch.round).
    #        np.squeeze collapses (1,1,H,W)->(H,W). If a custom export emits raw
    #        logits, set already_sigmoid=False. ---
    prob = np.squeeze(ll).astype(np.float32)           # (H,W)
    if not already_sigmoid:
        prob = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-prob))

    # --- 3. Remove letterbox padding if the keep-aspect path was used. The
    #        official [12:372] crop is NOT used here: it is hardcoded to the
    #        original 1280x720 letterbox geometry and is wrong for any other
    #        input shape. We strip the actual pad we added instead. ---
    if letterbox_pad is not None:
        dw, dh, _r = letterbox_pad
        H, W = prob.shape
        top = int(round(dh - 0.1)); bot = H - int(round(dh + 0.1))
        left = int(round(dw - 0.1)); right = W - int(round(dw + 0.1))
        top = max(top, 0); left = max(left, 0)
        bot = min(bot, H); right = min(right, W)
        prob = prob[top:bot, left:right]

    # --- 4. Threshold at 0.5 (== official torch.round on a [0,1] map). ---
    bin_mask = (prob > lane_threshold).astype(np.uint8)

    # --- 5. Resize back to the target HxW. NEAREST for the binary mask (keep it
    #        crisp/binary), LINEAR for the confidence channel. ---
    H_out, W_out = orig_hw
    bin_mask = cv2.resize(bin_mask, (W_out, H_out), interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST)
    conf = cv2.resize(prob, (W_out, H_out), interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)

    # --- 6. Class-id map (lane=lane_class_id, everything else 0) + uint8 conf. ---
    mask = (bin_mask * np.uint8(lane_class_id)).astype(np.uint8)
    conf = np.clip(conf * 255.0, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    return mask, conf
open_questions: DECODE CONFLICT RESOLVED IN FAVOR OF SINGLE-CHANNEL torch.round (not argmax): official CAIC-AD utils.py uses torch.round(ll).squeeze(1) — squeeze(1) on a size-2 axis would error, so the lane head IS 1-channel; the (1,2,H,W) figure is from the OLDER hustvl/YOLOP model and from YOLOPv2's DRIVABLE-AREA head. Backed by live source (verified 2026-06-01: utils.py + hpc203 np.squeeze). The brief's stated (1,2,H,W) for the LANE head is WRONG for YOLOPv2. Still: confirm session.get_outputs()[i].shape on YOUR actual .onnx before trusting — this is the #1 silent-garbage risk.

ONNX OUTPUT ORDER CONFLICT (resolved by name-introspection, not a pick): PINTO surgically-renamed graph exposes 'll' at index/name 'll' (1ch); Kazuhito00 raw torch.onnx.export flatten puts ll at INDEX 5 (6 outputs); hpc203 post-graph puts ll at index 1. ALL THREE verified from source. Because they genuinely differ, yolopv2.py must select by name 'll' / by 1-channel shape, NEVER a hardcoded index. Whichever ONNX file you actually ship determines the order — re-introspect after any re-export.

Whether ll arrives ALREADY sigmoid (in [0,1]) vs raw logits — could not empirically run the model. Code logic (torch.round / >0.5) strongly implies post-sigmoid baked into the graph, AND Kazuhito00's seg decode does 1.0-seg[0][0] (channel-0 prob, not argmax) reinforcing that activations are baked in differently per export. VERIFY on the laptop with CPU ORT: print(ll.min(), ll.max()); [0,1] => round path correct; ~[-10,10] => set already_sigmoid=False.

Exact filenames inside PINTO resources.tar.gz not byte-verified (Wasabi S3 not browsable). Inferred yolopv2_{H}x{W}.onnx + yolopv2_post_{H}x{W}.onnx from convert_script.txt naming + demo default. No native 480x300 model — use 288x480 (stretch) or export-it-yourself at 384x640.

No published YOLOPv2-on-Orin latency benchmark and no first-hand YOLOPv2-on-IGVC report exist — the latency estimate (~8-20ms) and the domain-gap verdict (likely_poor) are reasoned from comparable nets + training distribution + weak 27% in-domain IoU, not measured numbers. Validate both empirically on real IGVC frames before committing GPU budget away from the working classical pipeline.

fp16 (Jetson) vs fp32 (laptop) can flip borderline pixels around the 0.5 threshold — run a mask-parity check on a fixed frame before trusting the Jetson output as equivalent to the laptop-validated mask.

STRETCH vs LETTERBOX must be decided once: letterbox-to-384x640 is decode-faithful (and lets you keep the official semantics) but requires unletterbox math; plain-stretch matches the ONNX demos and is simpler but distorts aspect (tape geometry feeds the costmap reprojection). Do NOT mix the official [12:372]/x2 crop with a stretch path — that combination is silent garbage.

verdicts.claim: YOLOPv2 ONNX preprocessing is RGB (BGR->RGB flip required), NCHW (1,3,H,W), /255.0 only with NO ImageNet mean/std; official letterbox default is auto=True (pads to nearest stride-32 multiple) so a fixed-input ONNX/TRT engine must use auto=False or plain cv2.resize stretch+drop crop; detection decode uses sigmoid (skipped); official seg crops [12:372]. Verified across CAIC-AD demo.py, PINTO demo, hpc203 demo, Kazuhito00 sample.
verdicts.evidence: Official CAIC-AD/YOLOPv2 utils/utils.py LoadImages.__next__: `img = img[:, :, ::-1].transpose(2, 0, 1)  # BGR to RGB, to 3x416x416`; demo.py: `img /= 255.0` with no mean/std; letterbox default `auto=True` (https://github.com/CAIC-AD/YOLOPv2/blob/main/utils/utils.py, https://github.com/CAIC-AD/YOLOPv2/blob/main/demo.py). hpc203 onnxruntime/onnx/main.py L58-64: cv2.resize stretch + cvtColor(BGR2RGB) + transpose + /255.0, no mean/std, no [12:372] crop; L73 sigmoid `y = 1/(1+np.exp(-y))`. PINTO_model_zoo 326_YOLOPv2/demo/demo_yolopv2_post_onnx.py L15-21: identical cv.resize + cvtColor(BGR2RGB) + /255.0, no mean/std, no crop.
verdicts.correction: Substantively correct; one wording nuance: in the OFFICIAL .pt path the BGR->RGB flip (img[:, :, ::-1]) lives in the LoadImages dataloader in utils/utils.py, not literally in demo.py. The cited ONNX demos achieve the same with cv2.cvtColor(BGR2RGB). Also note seg crop is seg[:,:,12:372,:] (along the 384-row letterboxed height: 384-12-12=360 valid rows), which is exactly why the recommendation to letterbox to 384x640 keeps that crop valid — confirmed. No factual error affects the deployment recipe.

verdicts.claim: YOLOPv2 lane-line ('ll') output: export-specific position (PINTO/hpc203 index 1; Kazuhito00 index 5); shape (1,1,H,W) single-channel post-sigmoid; decoded by round / >0.5 threshold (do NOT re-sigmoid); (1,2,H,W) is the drivable-area head / older hustvl YOLOP, not the lane head; conf-thres/iou-thres are detection-NMS only and irrelevant to lanes.
verdicts.evidence: Official CAIC-AD/YOLOPv2 utils/utils.py: lane_line_mask -> `ll_seg_mask = torch.round(ll_seg_mask).squeeze(1)`; driving_area_mask -> `_, da_seg_mask = torch.max(da_seg_mask, 1)` (DA is the 2-channel/argmax head, lane is round-thresholded). hpc203 onnxruntime/onnx/main.py: `drivable_area = np.squeeze(results[0]...)` -> `np.argmax(...,axis=0)`; `lane_line = np.squeeze(results[1])` -> `np.where(lane_line > 0.5, 1, 0)` (lane at index 1, threshold 0.5, no sigmoid); detection heads results[2..4] get explicit `1/(1+np.exp(-y))`. Kazuhito00 sample.py: dets=results[0..3], road=results[4], lane=results[5]; utils_onnx.lane_line_mask returns `ll[0][0]` (batch0/channel0 -> channel dim==1), thresholded `>0.5` in visualization. demo.py unpacks `[pred,anchor_grid],seg,ll = model(img)` (name 'll').
verdicts.correction: Two minor, measure-zero inaccuracies in the claim's RATIONALE (conclusions stand): (1) 'squeeze(1) on a size-2 axis would error' is false — torch.Tensor.squeeze(dim) on a non-size-1 dimension is a SILENT NO-OP, not an error, so it does not by itself prove channel==1 (the single-channel conclusion is still correct, proven independently by torch.round being valid only on a [0,1] prob map, by hpc203 np.squeeze(results[1]) collapsing to (H,W), and by Kazuhito00 ll[0][0]). (2) torch.round uses round-half-to-even, so at exactly 0.5 it maps to 0, i.e. torch.round(ll) equals (ll > 0.5), not (ll >= 0.5) as written — inconsequential on a continuous sigmoid (half-point is measure-zero), as the claim itself notes. All operational facts (name 'll', positions 1 vs 5, single-channel (1,1,H,W) lane vs 2-channel (1,2,H,W) DA, 0.5 decode, already-post-sigmoid, NMS thresholds irrelevant to lanes) are correct.

verdicts.claim: At least one of the listed YOLOPv2 yolopv2.pt / ONNX download URLs is currently real and reachable; canonical is https://github.com/CAIC-AD/YOLOPv2/releases/download/V0.0.1/yolopv2.pt — GitHub release asset, tag V0.0.1, 156,380,200 bytes (~149.1 MiB), FP32 TorchScript loaded via torch.jit.load (not a state_dict); README states 38.9M params.
verdicts.evidence: curl -IL on https://github.com/CAIC-AD/YOLOPv2/releases/download/V0.0.1/yolopv2.pt: HTTP/2 302 -> 200, content-disposition: attachment; filename=yolopv2.pt, content-length: 156380200 (=149.136 MiB), last-modified 2022-08-30; first 4 bytes via range request = 504b 0304 (PK ZIP magic = TorchScript archive). demo.py (raw.githubusercontent.com/CAIC-AD/YOLOPv2/main/demo.py): `model = torch.jit.load(weights)` with weights default data/weights/yolopv2.pt. README: "**38.9M**" params and links exactly that release URL. PINTO mirror https://s3.ap-northeast-2.wasabisys.com/pinto-model-zoo/326_YOLOPv2/resources.tar.gz also returns HTTP/1.1 200 OK, Content-Type application/gzip.
verdicts.correction: All primary sub-claims verified. Two minor caveats (claim still CONFIRMED): (1) the README/demo do not literally use the word "FP32," but torch.jit.load + the PK-zip magic confirm it is a TorchScript archive (not a pickle state_dict) and TorchScript default export is FP32 — load mechanism is exactly as claimed. (2) The PINTO wasabi resources.tar.gz is the ENTIRE PINTO_model_zoo resources archive (Content-Length 15,802,890,311 = ~14.7 GiB), not a 326_YOLOPv2-only tarball; the URL resolves and serves a real gzip but is not scoped to just YOLOPv2, and its inner filenames/ONNX layout remain unverified (claim already flagged these as "inferred"/"NOT byte-verified"). The HuggingFace Space, Kazuhito00, and hpc203 URLs were not independently fetched, but the OR-claim is satisfied by the canonical GitHub URL alone.

verdicts.claim: On Jetson Orin/JetPack6, do NOT pip-install onnxruntime-gpu from PyPI (x86_64/win only, no aarch64 → CPU-only providers); use the NVIDIA Jetson AI Lab index jp6/cu126 (JetPack6+CUDA12.6, cp310 only) wheels, e.g. wget https://pypi.jetson-ai-lab.dev/jp6/cu126/+f/f6e/2baa664069470/onnxruntime_gpu-1.20.2-cp310-cp310-linux_aarch64.whl (newer 1.23.0/1.24.0 cp310 aarch64 also there); FIRST pip uninstall onnxruntime onnxruntime-gpu (CPU build shadows GPU, same import name); keep dev laptop on CPU onnxruntime; bake a startup assert 'CUDAExecutionProvider' in ort.get_available_providers().
verdicts.evidence: PyPI onnxruntime-gpu files page shows only manylinux_2_27/2_28_x86_64 + win_amd64, no linux_aarch64 (https://pypi.org/project/onnxruntime-gpu/#files); Ultralytics Jetson guide: "The onnxruntime-gpu package hosted in PyPI does not have aarch64 binaries for the Jetson" (https://docs.ultralytics.com/guides/nvidia-jetson/); jp6/cu126 onnxruntime-gpu page on pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io lists cp310 aarch64 wheels 1.23.0 and 1.24.0 (https://pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/jp6/cu126/onnxruntime-gpu); ONNX Runtime issue threads document CPU build shadowing GPU and the uninstall-both remedy (https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/issues/7748).
verdicts.correction: Two specifics are stale/wrong though the engineering thesis holds. (1) DOMAIN: the index is now pypi.jetson-ai-lab.IO, not .dev — the .dev host returns ECONNREFUSED and NVIDIA-forum threads confirm a .dev→.io migration; the claim's wget URL fails today. Use https://pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/jp6/cu126/ . (2) EXACT WHEEL/HASH unverified: the 1.20.2 hash path f6e/2baa664069470 returns 404 on .io (and .dev unreachable) — could not confirm from a primary source; the currently-listed versions are 1.23.0 (hash e1e/9e3dc2f4d5551) and 1.24.0, so resolve the live hash from the index rather than hard-coding 1.20.2. Also note jp6/cu126 suffered an Oct-2025 package-removal event (NVIDIA: limited resources) — verify the wheel is present before relying on it. Minor: the pip uninstall-first rule is community/issue-tracker guidance, not in the official onnxruntime.ai install docs.

verdicts.claim: Domain-gap verdict "likely_poor": a BDD100K-trained YOLOPv2 lane head will likely NOT cleanly segment 3-inch white tape on open asphalt from a low tilted camera.
verdicts.evidence: YOLOPv2 paper (arxiv 2208.11434): lane head trained/evaluated exclusively on BDD100K, "driver perspective view," with NO cross-domain/generalization results reported. BDD100K lane training masks are an 8-px band drawn on the CENTERLINE between a painted lane's two edges (test masks 2 px) — i.e. far-field dashcam road lanes, not isolated thin close-up tape. No primary source tests YOLOPv2 on tape/asphalt/low-tilt camera in either direction.
verdicts.correction: The DIRECTION of the verdict is well-supported and I could not refute it — every independent line of evidence (dashcam-only training viewpoint, centerline-of-wide-lane mask representation vs. a single 3-inch stripe, and the lane-detection literature's documented sharp cross-domain degradation driven primarily by camera pose/pitch/height) points to poor transfer. BUT it is a PREDICTION, not a measured result: no primary source empirically tests YOLOPv2 on 3-inch tape on open asphalt from a low tilted camera, so it cannot be marked CONFIRMED. Two caveats that should temper the verdict: (1) BDD100K's scene tags DO include parking lots/residential/asphalt with white markings, so plain-asphalt white lines are partially in-domain — the gap is dominated by camera POSE and line SCALE, not asphalt-vs-grass surface; (2) "likely_poor" is the correct hedge — keep "likely," do not harden to "will fail." Recommend treating it as a defensible engineering prior requiring a quick on-camera sanity test (or fine-tuning) before relying on it, rather than a verified fact.
